Assume that your network operates in a regulatory domain that allows use of the entire 5 GHz space allowed in the 802.11ac amendment. In your upcoming 802.11ac deployment, you would like to take advantage of the performance improvements that result from channel bonding. However, after extensive testing, you have determined that your mission-critical WLAN should not use channels requiring DFS support. Given those two criteria (enable channel bonding and disable DFS channels), in the 5 GHz spectrum, how many non-overlapping 40 MHz channels will your system be able to use?
C
Avoiding DFS channels leaves a smaller set of 5 GHz channels for bonding. The answer key's count is based on the non-DFS spectrum available in the stated regulatory domain.
What commonly causes a client-to-AP link imbalance?
The client's antenna gain is lower than the AP's antenna gain
The client's transmit power is significantly lower than the AP's transmit power
The AP's transmit power is significantly lower than the client's transmit power
The AP's antenna gain is lower than the client's antenna gain
B
A client usually transmits at lower power than an AP. The AP may therefore hear the client poorly even when the client can hear the AP, creating an asymmetric link.

You are on site, planning a network at a freight shipping company on a busy harbor. Since the preliminary WLAN design specifies support for the 5 GHz spectrum, you would like to test for radar pulses to determine if DFS channels should be supported at this facility. As a part of your spectral survey with a laptop-based analyzer, you include DFS testing to identify the presence of radar. This is done by manually observing Real-time FFT, Duty Cycle, and Active Devices charts of the spectrum analyzer software. What potential drawback is present with this DFS test method?
Many WLAN products that support DFS channels report several false positives. Ideally, the actual WLAN equipment used in the deployment should be used to test for DFS.
Some sources of 5 GHz radar, such as military ships, are mobile in nature. A longer, automated test setup should be used to identify the presence or absence of radar.
Manual identification of radar pulses using spectrum analysis charts can be very difficult due to radar's low amplitude at the Wi-Fi receiver.
Modern spectrum analyzer adapters do not provide the necessary bandwidth resolution required to detect and measure radar signatures.
C
Radar pulses can be difficult to identify manually because they may be brief and have low amplitude at the Wi-Fi receiver. A short visual walkthrough can miss intermittent radar activity.

When performing an indoor predictive site survey to make the WLAN planning and design cycle more efficient, what is a best practice for configuration of the simulated APs in the predictive modeling software?
All simulated APs should be set to 20 MHz channels only.
Always use the default 2.2 dBi omnidirectional antenna patterns for simulated APs.
If dynamic RRM will be used, AP transmit power should be set to an estimated average level of the expected client devices, such as 25 mW.
Defining custom AP and antenna patterns will yield more accurate prediction data than the preconfigured vendor AP/antenna combinations.
C
When dynamic RRM will manage transmit power, configure simulated APs near the expected average client/AP power level. This makes the predictive model a more realistic starting point.
What action should be taken after implementing a WLAN based on the design developed from the site survey process?
Post-installation survey
Requirements analysis
Gathering facility documentation
Design the infrastructure services
A
A post-installation survey checks the live WLAN against the design and requirements, revealing coverage, capacity, interference, and configuration issues before handoff.
When preparing a floor plan graphic for use in predictive and manual site surveying, what calibration method will lead to the most accurate and reliable RF data?
Use the known size of a small object, such as a ceiling tile, and use a single instance of this object (e.g. a single ceiling tile) to scale the floor plan.
Measure the width of an actual office doorway with a tape measure and use this value to calibrate against a doorway graphic.
Use the longest available measurement (like a straight exterior wall) to calibrate the graphic's scale.
Calibrate the ceiling height of the floor plan first, then the survey software should be able to auto-calibrate the X and Y planes of the graphic.
C
Calibrate the floor plan using the longest reliable known measurement, such as a straight exterior wall. A longer reference reduces the relative impact of measurement error.

While configuring your site survey software for an upcoming manual survey project, you notice the configuration option for "Network Card Simulation". What is the purpose of such a feature and when would you use it?

This setting allows the site survey software to convert the APs measured downlink RF data into a simulated data set as if the same data were transmitted by a specific client station. It is useful for determining uplink client performance when clients are located far from APs as well as projecting cell size for ad hoc networks.

Since WLAN adapters are not typically calibrated by manufacturers, this setting is a form of software calibration in which you can calibrate an (uncalibrated) adapter to match one of the calibrated adapters shown in the list. This process improves the reliability of RF data collection and reporting when uncalibrated adapters are used.

This is the configuration area in which you specify the adapter type that will be used for the site survey so that the survey software can interpret that adapters reported metrics (based on proprietary formulas) into an RF measurement that is standardized by the survey software and known to its users. This is done
A
Client emulation adjusts measured downlink data to estimate what a specific client would receive or achieve. This helps assess uplink/downlink imbalance and client-specific cell boundaries.

A wireless engineer from your company performed a site survey in an office building where a wireless network extension was needed. He reports that while performing a Layer 1 sweep near a meeting room full of people, he detected RF activity with a very low duty cycle. He is unsure how to interpret what he recorded to determine its impact on a future Wi-Fi network. What is true about this RF environment and its potential impact on the WLAN?
The signal affects the entire spectrum and will render the wireless network unusable. It must be located and removed.
The signal has a low duty cycle and should not be of major impact on the wireless network.
The signal is alternating between peaks (high interference level) and valleys (low interference level). The network channel design must be built to avoid the affected peak frequencies.
The signal is typical of a high radio card background noise. It shows that the card used for the Layer 1 sweep should be replaced and the Layer 1 sweep re-
B

A low-duty-cycle interferer occupies the channel only briefly. Its impact is usually limited compared with a continuous or high-duty-cycle source, though timing and application sensitivity still matter.
What is the meaning of a Real Time FFT graph?
Real Time FFT means Real Time First Fundamental Trace and shows the value of the first signal detected on each frequency at each sweep interval.
Real Time FFT means Real Time Fast Frequency Timing and shows the RF pulses measured by the Layer 1 sweep tool.
Real Time FFT means Real Time Fast Fourier Transform and shows the max value of the signal detected on each frequency in real time.
Real Time FFT means Real Time Frequency Fundamental Texture and shows the value of the noise background generated by the card used to perform the
Real Time FFT means Real Time Fast Fourier Transform and shows the max value of the signal detected on each frequency in real time.
C
A real-time FFT displays signal energy across frequency as it is being measured. It helps identify active RF energy and its frequency location.
In a PC-based spectrum analyzer, what data chart identifies the overall RF utilization of a specific frequency in the environment being surveyed?
FFT Max Hold
FFT Average
Swept Spectrogram
Duty cycle
C
A waterfall or spectrogram view plots RF energy over time, making intermittent or changing non-Wi-Fi interferers easier to identify.

Given: In a site survey deliverable report, you are expected to explain the spectrum measurements taken at the customers site. What portion of a spectrum analyzer view can be used to determine if a given channel is too active for use as the active channel for a new AP?
Device list
Frame decode
Real time FFT
Duty cycle
D
Duty cycle is the percentage of time an RF source is transmitting. It helps describe how much airtime an interferer occupies.

You are testing a VoWLAN deployment, and your communication measurements show a certain amount of lost packets. What would be an acceptable packet error rate value to still provide acceptable call quality?
There should be 0% error in a VoWLAN type of deployment
No more than 1% PER max should be acceptable
No more than 4% PER max should be acceptable
No more than 8% PER max should be acceptable
D
Packet error rate is a key voice-quality metric because lost packets can degrade speech. Use the stated maximum as the acceptance threshold for this question.

You are site surveying a network for VoWiFi. You have positioned an AP for a manual survey and are moving away from the AP with a phone in Survey Mode in your hand and you are reading the RSSI value of the signal received from the AP. You have previously determined that the noise floor was approximately -94 dBm on this floor of the building. The phones documentation does not specify a recommended RSSI or SNR value for best performance. Based on the information provided and the type of device (VoWiFi phone) you are deploying, what minimum RSSI should you plan for in all areas you are monitoring and where VoWiFi service is desired?
- 75 dBm
- 72 dBm
- 67 dBm
- 62 dBm
C
Voice WLAN designs commonly target about −67 dBm RSSI at the client to support reliable voice operation and roaming, subject to the design's SNR and device requirements.
What statement is true of a WLAN design that supports Real-Time Location Services (RTLS) with 802.11 RFID asset tags?
When passive tags are implemented, the AP density should be increased by 25% to make up for the shorter transmit range of passive tags as compared to active tags.
Active RFID tags periodically transmit 802.11 beacon management frames that must be synchronized with the AP for proper location of the tagged asset.

With passive tags, AP transmit gain should be increased to supply extra power for near-field coupling or backscatter modulation from the tag to the AP since the passive tag lacks an internal power source.
Passive tags do not communicate directly with the WLAN infrastructure, but instead they rely on the tag reader to communicate tag information to the
D
Passive RFID tags do not actively transmit Wi-Fi frames. A tag reader energizes or interrogates the tag and reports the tag's presence to the location system.

In this question, you will compare the mobility processes of a network that supports WPA2-Personal and WPA2-Enterprise. Assume the use of a 15-character ASCII passphrase for WPA2-Personal and EAP-TTLS/MSCHAPv2 with WPA2-Enterprise. Also, assume that proprietary roaming protocols are not supported. When a device transitions from one BSS to another within the same ESS, what step must be performed in the WPA2-Enterprise transition that are not performed in the WPA2-Personal transition?
Open System Authentication
802.11 Reassociation
802.1X authentication
4-Way Handshake
C

802.1X authentication requires an authentication exchange when the client associates, while a pre-shared key can avoid that per-user EAP exchange. The question contrasts the mobility behavior of these security methods.

ABC Manufacturing has a heavily-used dual-band (2.4 / 5 GHz) WLAN, but sporadic RF interference across the 2.4 GHz band is causing dropped VoWiFi calls and leading to data connectivity and throughput problems. In addition to avoiding 2.4 GHz channels and installing a distributed spectrum analyzer to locate RF interference sources, what should the implementer do to resolve the problem fully?
Have only guest access on the 5 GHz channels.
Move all corporate data clients and VoWiFi devices to the 5 GHz channels appropriate for their regulatory domain.
Use captive portals for guest authentication in 5 GHz.
Implement WPA-PSK everywhere in the network.
B
Moving corporate data and voice clients to supported 5 GHz channels removes them from the affected 2.4 GHz interference environment, provided their devices and coverage design support 5 GHz.
When you see the SKINNY protocol in a post-install validation protocol capture, what does this indicate?
Secure FTP is in use
VoIP is used on the network
HTTPS is in use
Multicasting is used on the network
B
Skinny Client Control Protocol (SCCP/SKINNY) is commonly used by IP phones for call signaling. Seeing it in the capture indicates that VoIP telephony is operating on the network.

During a post-deployment verification, you are requested to troubleshoot an area where users are experiencing poor throughput. They are using data communication only, mainly from laptops. You captured the frame showing an incorrect FCS. This frame is typical of those that were captured by the analyzer. What does this frame reveal about the RF network in this area?
One station seems to be streaming video, thus may have reserved significant bandwidth via admission control
Contention Free is in place in this network, which may starve some non-QoS stations from access
Multipath or excessive collisions seem to be an issue in this area
The AP seems to be too far to provide enough coverage to this area
C
Multipath and excessive collisions can cause retransmissions, variable latency, and poor application performance even when basic coverage appears adequate.
Excessive uplink RTP frame retransmissions can result in ____________.
Deauthentication of the transmitter by the receiver
Lowering of the data transmission rate by the transmitting station
MOS scores in excess of 5
Head-of-Line blocking at the receiver
B
Repeated RTP retransmissions indicate poor link conditions and consume airtime. Rate-control algorithms may respond by stepping down to a lower PHY rate.
When designing a WLAN to support voice in a large office, which design element is of the highest concern for performance?
Frequency Selection
Roaming
AP vendor
Band steering
B
Roaming performance depends on how quickly a client can move between APs and complete reassociation. Delays or interruptions are especially noticeable to voice applications.
